mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates on future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8.0% over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases the likelihood of a recession and triggers risk-off behavior in equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts and retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to downward revisions in equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production below 95.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real economic output, which increases the probability of a recession and triggers equity market sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX shows positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts above 700,000 units combined with rising retail sales signals strong consumer confidence and expanding demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 227.0 combined with a flat or declining federal funds rate signals a failure of monetary policy to contain price pressures, increasing the risk of stagflation and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the interaction effect has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below 132,000 in a single month signals a sudden labor market contraction, which increases recession risk and triggers equity market sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (measured via RSAFS) combined with rising housing starts indicates strong underlying demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, particularly in a low-inflation environment.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
